first.rationale: Both onboarding completion and activation are down 4-6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 directly address onboarding simplification and completion—both showed durable lifts in adoption. This is a lower-risk play than promotional_pricing (which memory_73 showed damages retention despite acquisition gains) or referral_incentives (which require established customer base we're losing engagement from). Enterprise_sales_assist addresses a different segment. Verifying these two memories will confirm the magnitude and durability of prior onboarding gains before scaling. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a secondary consideration but onboarding completion is the upstream lever. This preserves optionality on referral incentives for Q4 and avoids the retention trap of pricing pressure.

final.rationale: Archive confirms both memories. Memory_31 showed +9% activation lift and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention risk. Memory_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value improvement, and +3% retention gain. Current situation shows 4-6% declines in both completion and activation QoQ. Simplifying onboarding directly addresses both metrics and carries retention upside (memory_86) rather than downside. This is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (memory_73 flagged material retention damage) and better targeted than enterprise_sales_assist (which serves a different conversion path). The verification confirms durability. Standard_experiment scale allows measurement without full rollout risk, preserving option value on referral incentives or messaging if needed. Primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue is best served by fixing the upstream funnel leak.
